newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador, Peru suspend border talks over crisis.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador, Peru suspend border talks over crisis.

text.p: Ecuador and Peru Wednesday called off border talks scheduled for Friday due to the hostage crisis in Lima, Ecuador's Deputy Foreign Minister Diego Ribadeneira said.

"I've just received a call from Peruvian Deputy Foreign Minister Jorge Boto Vernales telling me that because of the events taking place in Peru, they've decided to suspend the meeting," Ribadeneira told reporters. "We agreed and will reschedule the talks."

On Tuesday night Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela was taken hostage by leftist guerrillas with at least 200 other men, including diplomats and businessmen, attending a reception at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The rebels are demanding the release of 400 to 500 jailed comrades and safe passage to an Amazon jungle hideout.

Peruvian and Ecuadoran officials had planned to meet in the Brazilian capital on Friday to resume negotiations in a longstanding border dispute which led their countries to a jungle war early last year. The peace talks are being monitored by the United States, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.
